In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NMR chemical shifts of the C2 atom are not a reliable measure of the strength or the bonding mechanism of hydrogen bonding in A-T and A-uracil base pairs.
the C2- and C4-atom chemical shifts are influenced in different ways and to different extents by the nature of the substituent, the environment, and the hydrogen-bonding strength.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the hydrogen-bonding mechanism and the hydrogen-bond length are important, they are not sufficient to explain the NMR shielding changes in the supramolecular complexes.
the C2-atom shielding is influenced by the environment and the nature of the substituent.
the NMR shielding constant of a C2 atom is determined by the electronic properties of the C2 atom itself and its substituent, and not by the hydrogen-bonding strength.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C2- and C4-adenine shielding constants are not reliable indicators of changes in the hydrogen bond.
the C2-atom chemical shift is a sensitive probe of the hydrogen-bonding strength and the environment of the base pairs.
the C2-atom NMR shielding constants are strongly dependent on the nature and position of the substituent.
